## Features

What the system does. Each feature is proven at the levels it requires.

| Feature | What it does | `conformance` | `concurrency` | `versioning` | `faults` | `compatibility` | `security` | `operations` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server.start` | The first start creates the superuser and the postgres database, then accepts connections. | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — | ⬜ |
| `server.config.file` | A config.yaml sets the data directory, listener, users and behavior. | — | — | — | — | — | — | ⬜ |
| `server.config.env` | DOLTGRES_USER, DOLTGRES_PASSWORD and DOLTGRES_DATA_DIR configure a first start. | — | — | — | — | — | — | ⬜ |
| `server.docker` | The dolthub/doltgresql image runs the server with its documented environment. | — | — | — | — | — | — | ⬜ |
| `server.database.create` | CREATE DATABASE makes a new database, each its own Dolt repository. | ⬜ | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| `server.database.drop` | DROP DATABASE removes a database. | ⬜ | — | — | — | — | — | — |
| `server.restart` | A clean restart keeps every committed change. | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — | ⬜ |
| `server.gc` | dolt_gc() reclaims unreferenced storage. | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — | ⬜ |
| `server.metrics` | The server exports the metrics its docs list. | — | — | — | — | — | — | ⬜ |
| `client.connect` | A client connects over the PostgreSQL wire protocol with password authentication. | — | — | — | ⬜ | ⬜ | — | — |
| `client.query.simple` | The simple query protocol runs statements and returns rows. | — | — | — | ⬜ | ⬜ | — | — |
| `client.query.extended` | The extended protocol prepares, binds and executes statements. | — | — | — | ⬜ | ⬜ | — | — |
| `client.bind.typed` | Bind parameters with declared types are read as those types. | — | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — |
| `client.bind.untyped` | Untyped bind parameters are inferred as PostgreSQL infers them. | — | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — |
| `client.bind.binary` | Parameters and results in binary format round-trip. | — | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — |
| `client.copy.from` | COPY ... FROM STDIN loads rows. | — | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — |
| `client.copy.to` | COPY ... TO STDOUT writes rows. | — | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — |
| `client.error.fields` | An error carries its SQLSTATE and the schema, table, column and constraint fields. | — | — | — | — | ⬜ | — | — |

## Invariants

What the system must never do, or must always do, for each subject it applies to.

### `database` invariants

Where a row names several levels, each cell shows one mark per level, in that order.

- <a id="inv-access.branch_control_enforced"></a>**`access.branch_control_enforced`** · access — Writing to a branch without permission is refused on every path, including dolt_merge, dolt_reset, cherry-pick and revert.
- <a id="inv-access.denied_no_effect"></a>**`access.denied_no_effect`** · access — A statement refused for privileges changes nothing and reports the refusal.
- <a id="inv-access.history_respects_grants"></a>**`access.history_respects_grants`** · access — History, diff, blame and AS OF never expose rows of a table the role cannot read.
- <a id="inv-access.least_privilege"></a>**`access.least_privilege`** · access — A role reads and writes only what it was granted, and REVOKE takes effect for new statements.
- <a id="inv-backup.gc_keeps_reachable"></a>**`backup.gc_keeps_reachable`** · sharing — Garbage collection never loses a reachable commit or row.
- <a id="inv-backup.restore_equal"></a>**`backup.restore_equal`** · sharing — A restore equals the database at the backup point.
- <a id="inv-catalog.matches_postgres"></a>**`catalog.matches_postgres`** · answers — information_schema and pg_catalog describe a schema as PostgreSQL does for the same DDL.
- <a id="inv-client.clear_failure"></a>**`client.clear_failure`** · durability — With the server down or slow, a client gets an error within its timeout, never a hang.
- <a id="inv-client.driver_standard_flow"></a>**`client.driver_standard_flow`** · compatibility — Each documented driver connects, prepares, binds every supported type, runs transactions and reads back equal values.
- <a id="inv-client.no_double_apply"></a>**`client.no_double_apply`** · durability — A statement whose connection dropped is applied once or not at all.
- <a id="inv-durability.commit_survives_crash"></a>**`durability.commit_survives_crash`** · durability — A committed transaction survives kill -9 and a restart.
- <a id="inv-durability.no_partial_after_crash"></a>**`durability.no_partial_after_crash`** · durability — After a crash, no transaction is half applied, and every branch head is a valid commit.
- <a id="inv-import.roundtrip_lossless"></a>**`import.roundtrip_lossless`** · compatibility — A pg_dump from PostgreSQL restores into Doltgres, and every row and value compares equal.
- <a id="inv-query.errors_match"></a>**`query.errors_match`** · answers — Input PostgreSQL rejects is rejected with the same SQLSTATE class, never silently accepted or altered.
- <a id="inv-query.matches_postgres"></a>**`query.matches_postgres`** · answers — A supported statement returns the rows, types and NULLs PostgreSQL returns for the same data, in the same order when ORDER BY fixes it.
- <a id="inv-replication.no_lost_commit"></a>**`replication.no_lost_commit`** · sharing — A commit the primary acknowledged reaches every replica after recovery, failover included.
- <a id="inv-replication.replica_consistent"></a>**`replication.replica_consistent`** · sharing — A replica never shows a half-applied commit.
- <a id="inv-schema.constraint_enforced"></a>**`schema.constraint_enforced`** · schema — Every declared constraint holds on every write path: INSERT, UPDATE, upsert, COPY, merge and cherry-pick.
- <a id="inv-schema.ddl_atomic"></a>**`schema.ddl_atomic`** · schema — A failed DDL statement leaves no partial change.
- <a id="inv-schema.ddl_preserves_data"></a>**`schema.ddl_preserves_data`** · schema — ALTER changes existing values only as PostgreSQL would.
- <a id="inv-schema.index_transparent"></a>**`schema.index_transparent`** · schema — An index never changes a query's result.
- <a id="inv-schema.sequence_unique"></a>**`schema.sequence_unique`** · schema — nextval never returns a value twice, under concurrency too, and respects setval.
- <a id="inv-server.no_panic"></a>**`server.no_panic`** · answers — No statement panics the server or ends the connection with an internal error.
- <a id="inv-server.upgrade_preserves"></a>**`server.upgrade_preserves`** · sharing — A database written by the previous release opens and reads the same on the new one.
- <a id="inv-sql.unsupported_fails_clean"></a>**`sql.unsupported_fails_clean`** · answers — An unsupported statement fails with a clear error and changes nothing.
- <a id="inv-txn.atomic"></a>**`txn.atomic`** · transactions — A rolled-back or failed transaction leaves no effect.
- <a id="inv-txn.bank_conserved"></a>**`txn.bank_conserved`** · transactions — Concurrent transfers preserve the total.
- <a id="inv-txn.constraints_under_race"></a>**`txn.constraints_under_race`** · transactions — Unique and foreign keys hold under concurrent writers.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_circular_info"></a>**`txn.no_circular_info`** · transactions — G1c: no cycle of transactions each seeing the other's writes.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_dirty_read"></a>**`txn.no_dirty_read`** · transactions — G1a and G1b: no transaction reads uncommitted or aborted data.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_dirty_write"></a>**`txn.no_dirty_write`** · transactions — G0: no write overwrites another transaction's uncommitted write.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_lost_update"></a>**`txn.no_lost_update`** · transactions — P4: a committed update is never overwritten by a stale read-modify-write.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_read_skew"></a>**`txn.no_read_skew`** · transactions — G-single: repeatable read and above read one snapshot.
- <a id="inv-txn.no_write_skew"></a>**`txn.no_write_skew`** · transactions — G2-item: serializable prevents write skew.
- <a id="inv-txn.visible_after_commit"></a>**`txn.visible_after_commit`** · transactions — After COMMIT returns, every new transaction sees its writes.
- <a id="inv-vc.branch_isolated"></a>**`vc.branch_isolated`** · versioning — Writes on one branch are invisible on another until merged, across sessions.
- <a id="inv-vc.branch_ops_atomic"></a>**`vc.branch_ops_atomic`** · versioning — A failed branch operation leaves no branch, tag or permission row behind.
- <a id="inv-vc.commit_atomic"></a>**`vc.commit_atomic`** · versioning — dolt_commit records exactly the committed state at that moment, never half of a concurrent transaction.
- <a id="inv-vc.diff_complete"></a>**`vc.diff_complete`** · versioning — A diff between two commits lists exactly the rows that differ between their snapshots.
- <a id="inv-vc.history_immutable"></a>**`vc.history_immutable`** · versioning — A commit's content never changes: AS OF a commit always returns the same rows.
- <a id="inv-vc.merge_constraints"></a>**`vc.merge_constraints`** · versioning — A merge result satisfies the constraints, or each violation is recorded and reported.
- <a id="inv-vc.merge_no_silent_loss"></a>**`vc.merge_no_silent_loss`** · versioning — A merge keeps both sides' changes, or reports a conflict or a violation. It never drops a change silently.
- <a id="inv-vc.push_atomic"></a>**`vc.push_atomic`** · sharing — A failed push leaves the remote at its old head.
- <a id="inv-vc.remote_equal"></a>**`vc.remote_equal`** · sharing — A clone, pull or fetch equals the source at that commit, row for row and by hash.
- <a id="inv-vc.reset_restores"></a>**`vc.reset_restores`** · versioning — reset --hard returns the working set exactly to HEAD.
- <a id="inv-vc.revert_inverse"></a>**`vc.revert_inverse`** · versioning — Reverting a commit restores what it changed, when nothing later conflicts.
- <a id="inv-vc.schema_scoped"></a>**`vc.schema_scoped`** · versioning — Version-control functions act on the named schema's table, not another schema's.

### `txn.isolation`

The isolation levels PostgreSQL defines (postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html). A supported level prevents every anomaly PostgreSQL's docs say it prevents; an unsupported one is refused when requested.

| Member | `doltgres.main` | `doltgres.release` | `postgres.reference` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read committed` | ⬜ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `repeatable read` | ⬜ | ❌ | ✅ |
| `serializable` | ⬜ | ❌ | ✅ |

## Exemptions and refusals

Each ☑️ and ⛔, with the reason and the test that proves it.

- `doltgres.main` × `txn.no_read_skew`: exempt. The claim is about repeatable read and serializable. The Doltgres docs (concepts/sql/transaction) say Doltgres uses the Read Committed transaction model, so it must refuse both levels when asked. Proven by `txn.hermitage/doltgres.main/txn.no_read_skew`.
- `doltgres.main` × `txn.no_write_skew`: exempt. The claim is about serializable, which the Doltgres docs say Doltgres does not offer, so it must refuse it when asked. Proven by `txn.hermitage/doltgres.main/txn.no_write_skew`.
- `doltgres.release` × `txn.no_read_skew`: exempt. The claim is about repeatable read and serializable. The Doltgres docs (concepts/sql/transaction) say Doltgres uses the Read Committed transaction model, so it must refuse both levels when asked. Proven by `txn.hermitage/doltgres.release/txn.no_read_skew`.
- `doltgres.release` × `txn.no_write_skew`: exempt. The claim is about serializable, which the Doltgres docs say Doltgres does not offer, so it must refuse it when asked. Proven by `txn.hermitage/doltgres.release/txn.no_write_skew`.
